## Open

### F-334 — A passing Storybook run rewrites 22 committed markup snapshots

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-log · open_

Running `npm run storybook:test:ci` in tools/blong-log leaves the working tree dirty: the runner
writes src/client/__markup_snapshots__/*.json on every run from .storybook/test-runner.cjs, which is
an analysis artifact and not a jest comparison, so what it writes depends on the browser it ran
with. Chromium 1243 serializes a computed style as `overflow: clip` where the committed file says
`visible`, so one run produced 22 modified files that a commit would have to explain and that no
assertion depends on. The 21 image snapshots in __image_snapshots__ are the comparison that matters;
those passed. Worth either listing the markup snapshots in .gitignore or normalising the style
properties they carry, so a local run does not hand the author a diff they did not ask for.

### F-531 — The CI storybook leg served a dev server whose output went into the log

> _2026-10-15 · tools/blong-log · open_

`tools/blong-log` was the only package whose `ci-test` ran a Storybook dev server: the chain
`blong-dev test || …; node --run storybook:test:ci` started `storybook dev`, so the CI log carried
the server's banner and its Vite build chatter next to the test results — the "not aligned with the
rest" the package's own skill already describes the other way round ("build static → serve → test →
exit"). `core/blong-browser` has the same script but never calls it from `ci-test`, which is why it
never showed.

The script now runs `storybook dev --ci --quiet --loglevel warn` with its output redirected to a
temp file, and prints that file only when the test runner fails — the log carries the tests'
results, and the server's output is still there for the failure that needs it. Verified by running
the script: 22 story tests pass and no banner or Vite line reaches the log.

Fixing the server left the larger half: the runner's own report — a `PASS` line, every story with
its `✓ smoke-test`, and jest's summary — was most of the log. It now goes to
`.ci-report/storybook.log`, which the workflow already uploads with `tools/*/.ci-report`; the script
prints one summary line and that path, and dumps the file when the runner fails, which is the shape
the tap leg already has. The runner also needs `FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1`: jest colours the
`Test Suites:` label, so an anchored grep matched nothing and the first attempt printed an empty
summary line. Verified end to end: two lines for the storybook leg, 22 tests and 21 snapshots
passing, tap 82 pass.

### F-541 — The storybook runner takes fewer options than it lists

> _2026-10-16 · tools/blong-log · open_

The runner validates its options against an allow-list, so the options jest itself would accept are
rejected with the runner's help text and a pointer to its issue tracker: `--reporters jest-junit`
and the equals form `--outputFile=<path>` both died that way, while `--json --outputFile <path>`
(the space form) is accepted and writes exactly the file a report bridge can read. The hooks are
narrower than they look too: the context `postVisit` is handed carries only `id`, `title`, `name`
and `hasFailure` — no story parameters — so a story cannot declare how long it needs before it is at
rest, and the runner keeps that list itself (`SETTLE_MS` in `.storybook/test-runner.cjs`). That wait
is what makes the shot a property of the rendering rather than of the machine: a story still
streaming rows when the shot is taken is compared against however many rows the runner delivered.
Probing an option costs a full storybook run, so try the space form of a jest option before
concluding the runner does not support it.

### F-788 — A taken UDP port killed the process instead of failing the start

> _2026-11-21 · tools/blong-log · open_

A container whose UDP port is already taken died with an unhandled `EADDRINUSE` instead of the
adapter's `start` failing. `UdpReceiver.start` bound the socket and subscribed `error` to
`this.emit('error', err)` — and an EventEmitter with no listener for `error` throws, so the emit
itself is the crash. The adapter in `realm/blong-viewer` subscribes to nothing but `start`'s
promise, which never got the chance to reject, and the pod restarted with a Node stack trace that
named the socket rather than the two listeners that collided.

The shape now: the socket's `error` listener reports only when somebody subscribed
(`listenerCount('error') > 0`), the bind's own `once('error', reject)` is removed when the bind
succeeds — a `once` left attached would swallow the first error of a running receiver — and `stop()`
tolerates a socket whose bind failed, because a stop after a failed start is a caller cleaning up.

The test is the second listener on one port, and it is cheap to keep:
`t.rejects(second.start(), /EADDRINUSE/)` fails loudly if the emit ever becomes unconditional again,
because the process would die instead of the assertion failing.

## Resolved

### F-773 — The log viewer could not be started or opened, and no test noticed

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

Reviewing `tools/blong-log` against lukaot turned up three defects that no test covered, because
each one is outside what the package tests: its producer was a pino transport and the framework had
stopped writing through pino, so the server had nothing feeding it; `public/index.html` did not
exist in any environment, so `/` answered 404 and the UI could not be opened at all; and its local
imports used `.js` specifiers that only the tap loader resolves, so the documented `npx blong-log`
could not start.

None of the three failed a test, and none would fail one now unless a test opened the page or
started the CLI. That is the lesson: a tool with a rendered surface needs one test that starts it
the way a person does and asks for what a person asks for — the page, and an entry in it. The e2e
test written with this change does the second half (a lukaot writer feeding the server, read back
through the API); the first is the remaining gap and is recorded as a todo.

Closed: producer moved to a lukaot writer with an e2e test, index.html added, .ts/.tsx specifiers,
request-derived addresses; the CLI smoke test is T-742.

### F-774 — An expanded grid row was measured, so it flickered and clipped its own detail

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The grid has to be told a row's height as data, not as a function: `rowHeight` on the column config
is one number for every row, and a function is silently ignored, which is why the expanded rows were
drawn at the theme's default and the detail was clipped. `rowHeight` on the row object is read, and
`_rowHeightFromData` makes the virtual scroller add up the same per-row heights — without it the
scroll range is computed from the default and an expanded row near the end cannot be reached.

`autoRowHeight` measures the rendered cell instead. That is what made an expanded row scrolled out
of view come back collapsed for a frame: it is drawn at its closed height, then it jumps when the
measurement lands, so the scroller repositions itself and a scroll gesture over that row can stop
working. The height is therefore derived from the record alone — bytes for a frame, lines for a
document — and never measured; the detail scrolls inside its own viewport instead.

Three more things this cost, all visible rather than diagnosed. A cell has to be the line plus the
padding or its text is cut in half: the theme pads a cell by 8px and sets a 20px line height, so the
28px row that looked dense was clipping every column, and the fix is a 16px line, 4px padding and a
26px row. `white-space: pre-wrap` on an expanded cell renders the newlines and indents between the
JSX elements as lines, which is the band of blank space that appeared above the first panel — it
belongs on the text that needs it. And the message and the JSON expand separately: one set of
expanded ids meant opening a record's JSON also opened its sentence.

Keyboard: space toggles the detail of the column the focused cell belongs to, read from the cell's
`data-col-id` (written with a leading colon, as `data-row-id` is) rather than from the grid's state,
which reports cells and rows under keys this version does not document.

### F-798 — The log page reconnects and refetches every five seconds

> _2026-11-21 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The deployed page asks for the watch stream and then a find every five seconds while the store holds
the same 27 records and the same last id, so both calls report nothing new. The five seconds is the
page's intervalMs, and the component uses it only after the subscription has ended, so what a reader
sees is a reconnect cycle rather than a subscription. Each re-subscription makes it worse: the page
subscribes with an empty cursor, and viewer.entry.watch yields its initial frame whenever the
requested after differs from the buffer's last id, so every reconnect delivers a wake carrying a
cursor the page already had, which costs one find. Two things are wrong and they are separable: the
stream is not surviving the first frame, which is what puts the page back on the timer, and a
reconnect cannot say where it got to, so the first frame of every subscription is spent re-learning
it. The second is fixable in the page by passing the last id it has; the first needs the stream to
stay open, and until it does a five-second poll is the honest description of what the page is doing.

Resolved in core/blong-gogo: loop.ts hands an async iterable back untouched, so the gateway's stream
route receives frames instead of a serialised value; the viewer page also passes its cursor, and the
deployed page now holds one open subscription with one wake per new record (verified on
marine.feasible.one: wakes 1 to 2 on a single record, unchanged over 15s of nothing).

### F-795 — A component's stylesheet was imported by the app entry

> _2026-11-21 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The grid stylesheet was imported by the standalone app entry beside the component, not by the
component. The standalone page was styled because it loads that entry; the portal mounts LogViewer
directly, so it drew the grid markup with no rules, columns collapsed onto each other and every row
overlapped the next, which reads as a broken page rather than as a page missing a stylesheet. A
component a host can mount on its own carries its styles with it; the import moved into
LogViewer.tsx and esbuild still emits app.css for the standalone page.

Done: LogViewer.tsx imports the grid stylesheet itself, and the portal page columns align — verified
on the deployed page, where the grid previously drew overlapping rows.

### F-797 — The grid's icons came from a third-party CDN

> _2026-11-21 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The grid component draws its carets, sort arrows, close marks and drag handles with wxi classes
whose glyphs come from a stylesheet it links from cdn.svar.dev, and its Willow themes name Open Sans
and Roboto through font faces pointed at the same host. The portal serves style-src self, so the
browser blocked the stylesheet and every icon drew as an empty box, and a deployment that faces the
internet would otherwise depend on a third party being reachable for its own UI. The theme
components take a fonts prop: rendering them with fonts false removes the link entirely, and the
classes the grid emits are mapped to PrimeIcons, which the portal already ships, in a stylesheet the
component imports after the vendor one. The grid's UI font follows the page through wx-font-family
inherit, because naming Roboto or Open Sans anywhere re-arms the web face. Bundling those fonts also
needed file loaders in build-client.js: esbuild has none for woff, woff2, ttf, eot or svg, and the
vendor stylesheet's last fallback spells the file primeicons.svg?#primeicons.

Done: the theme renders with fonts false (no CDN stylesheet), the wxi classes map to PrimeIcons in
gridIcons.css, and primeicons is a dependency with the font loaders esbuild needs. Verified on the
deployed page: no blocked stylesheet, icons drawn from the portal's own font.

Done: the theme renders with fonts false, so the CDN stylesheet is never requested, and the wxi
classes are mapped to PrimeIcons in gridIcons.css. One part is not: the browser still _asks_ for six
font files, because the portal's own font stack names Roboto and the vendor stylesheet declares a
face for it. They are refused by the deployment's CSP and never render, and the residual is tracked
as its own todo rather than claimed here.

### F-805 — The storybook shots were serif: fonts off means the host names the font

> _2026-11-21 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The Storybook screenshots and the CI comparison disagreed after the CDN-free icon change: the shots
came out in Times. The cause is the prop that fix introduced: the grid's theme is mounted with
fonts={false}, and that prop makes the vendor blank its own font family — three rules
declare --wx-font-family, the last with an empty value — so font-family: var(--wx-font-family) is
invalid and the text inherits the browser default, which is a serif. It is by design: with the
vendor's stylesheet off the network, the host supplies the typography, and the portal does
(PrimeReact's theme sets --font-family on the body, which the grid inherits). Only the Storybook
page had no font, because the preview's style block set margins and heights and nothing else. The
lesson is that a visual test measures whatever the page computes, including a font nobody named, and
that turning a vendor's stylesheet off also turns off the scale it carried: the fix is a font-family
in the preview, the stack the portal's own theme declares, so a story renders what an embedded
viewer renders.

Closed with the fix it produced: the Storybook preview names the portal's font stack, so font-family
resolves instead of falling back to a serif; the 27 image baselines were regenerated from that
rendering and the suite is green (28 tests, 27 snapshots).
